body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Monday, August 17, 2026 — a day that starts with a high of 99° and air quality at a moderate 55. Overnight, a group of juveniles with a firearm on Monterey Street was the headline call, and we’ll have more on that in a moment. For now, pour some coffee and let’s catch up on the night, the news, and the week ahead.

## The Kern Overnight

The night’s most serious call came around 11 p.m., when a group of five juveniles — one of whom pointed a firearm at the reporting party — was reported on Monterey Street. All were described as wearing dark clothing, and though no shots were fired, units were responding as the feed moved on. Earlier, shortly before 9:40 p.m., a possible shots-fired incident had units checking local hospitals for gunshot victims and looking for a suspect vehicle, though the exact location was unclear on the air. Fire crews also handled a one-acre grass fire near the bike path off Oak Street just after 10:30 p.m., with a slow rate of spread. In other incidents, multiple units responded to a domestic violence call in progress on Animas Court at 9:54 p.m., and an ex-boyfriend reportedly smashed a vehicle windshield with a shotgun in the FoodMaxx parking lot on Ming Avenue around 11:03 p.m. The small hours ran quieter, with the usual spread of disturbances, medical aids, and welfare checks.

## Today's weather

Today’s forecast calls for a high near 99° and a low around 73° tonight. It’s currently 88° at Meadows Field (KBFL), and the National Weather Service in Hanford has issued a Lake Wind Advisory until 8:00 p.m. this evening. Air quality is moderate at an AQI of 55. No active fires are reported in the county at this time.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that five vehicles were impounded during a northwest Bakersfield checkpoint and saturation patrol over the weekend.** The operation, which aimed to crack down on unsafe driving and unlicensed vehicles, also resulted in several citations and a DUI arrest. This enforcement effort underscores the ongoing push to improve road safety in the area.

**According to 23ABC, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. recently toured a Bakersfield program that he believes could reshape how schools teach children about food and nutrition.** Kennedy visited Edible Schoolyard Kern County, a program that brings gardening and cooking into the school curriculum. Students grow their own food in school gardens and then use that fresh produce in kitchen lessons. The goal is to connect classroom learning with what ends up on their plates, and Kennedy said the program’s focus on fresh food — including school cafeterias buying fresh produce — could be a model for schools nationwide.

**KGET 17 also shared that a Bakersfield police sergeant has been appointed as the next Kern County District Attorney’s chief of investigations.** The move highlights the close working relationship between local law enforcement and the DA’s office, and it’s expected to bring a wealth of experience to the role.

**In other news from KGET 17, the Kern County Sheriff’s Office arrested four individuals on various gun and drug possession charges after a copper wire theft.** The incident underscores the ongoing challenges with property crime in the county and the collaborative efforts by law enforcement to address it.

**23ABC reported on Bakersfield’s police and fire chiefs sharing their Fourth of July findings at a recent meeting, revealing both progress and ongoing concerns about fireworks-related incidents in the city.** Bakersfield Fire Chief Kevin Albertson noted that the holiday brought serious consequences for people across the state, with a total of 106 citations issued by the Bakersfield Police and Fire departments combined. Despite a 6% decrease in fire-related responses compared to 2025, officials say more work remains to deter illegal fireworks use.

## Something good

On a brighter note, Carlos Baldovinos — executive director of the Mission at Kern County — recently helped shape a federal best practices toolkit aimed at addressing addiction treatment within the homeless community. Baldovinos was among roughly 22 professionals from across the country who gathered in Washington, D.C., to develop the toolkit with the Trump administration, the Department of Housing and Urban Development, and the Department of Health and Human Services. The toolkit outlines best practices for working with individuals dealing with addiction, covering topics like program length, transitional housing, and long-term mentorship. It’s a proud moment for Kern County to be at the forefront of such important work.

## Coming up this week

Looking ahead, there are several public meetings and events worth noting this week. On Tuesday, August 18, the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee meets at 12:00 p.m., followed by the Historic Preservation Commission at 4:00 p.m. and the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission at 2:00 p.m. On Wednesday, August 19, the Water Board convenes at 10:00 a.m. Later in the week, the Planning Commission meets on Thursday, August 20, at 5:30 p.m.

For entertainment, the Fox Theater has a busy lineup. On Saturday, August 22, catch Los Yonic’s Zamacona, Los Caminantes, and Grupo Yndio. On Tuesday, August 24, the Cults & Classics: Season Pass 2026-2027 goes on sale. Later in the week, Rodney Carrington takes the stage on Thursday, August 27, followed by Cumbiatron: The Cumbia Rave on Friday, August 28. Willie Barcena performs on Saturday, August 29, and Michael Return of the King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix also takes place that evening.

That’s your brief for this Monday morning. Stay cool out there, and we’ll see you back here tomorrow.
